output.subject: We've received your complaint about your auto loan application
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us. We have received your complaint, and we want you to know that it has been read carefully.

You told us that you applied for an auto loan at the Sawmill Pkwy branch on Wednesday, September 16. You had a 768 credit score and nine years with the same hospital, and you were putting $4,000 down on a used SUV. You mentioned that the loan officer barely looked at your application. You also said he asked you twice where you were "originally from" and whether your green card was "permanent," although you are a US citizen. You told us that two days later you received a denial letter citing "insufficient credit history," and that a coworker with a lower score was approved at the same branch last month. You have asked us to tell you the real reason your application was denied.

We understand how upsetting this experience has been, and we're sorry for the distress it has caused you. A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days.

Thank you for bringing this to our attention.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The customer alleges national origin discrimination by a named-branch loan officer. Confirm this has gone to the appropriate specialist team before sending.
Confirm the September 16 application date and the date of the denial letter.
The customer disputes the stated denial reason, 'insufficient credit history', and is asking for the real reason. The specialist team should decide what can be disclosed.
The customer says they are a US citizen and was asked about green card status. Do not comment on this in the acknowledgment.
The coworker comparison involves a third party. Do not reference or discuss another customer's application.
The customer gave a phone number, but the reply is by email. Check whether they prefer to be contacted by phone.
